speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your condition, could you tell me if you experience any ringing in your ears or hearing loss? Also, does your dizziness worsen when you turn your head quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful information; your description of a constant, low-grade spinning sensation rather than episodic vertigo is unusual for typical inner ear issues. Have you noticed any new neurological symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, weakness in your arms or legs, or difficulty walking straight?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral Labyrinthitis. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Internal Auditory Canals and Brainstem. REQUEST TEST: Audiometry.
